headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from MinerU-to-pipecat document/audio handoff; no direct shared-channel evidence, but default docs imply an inference pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes MCP/REST surfaces, while pipecat has shared-bus, websocket, and LLM/vision integrations. A plausible bridge exists if MinerU output is fed into pipecat prompts or tools, but no direct shared channel is documented here. Uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into pipecat prompts or tool messages without sanitization
IF a shared MCP or websocket bridge is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Add an explicit prompt/content delimiter before passing MinerU text to pipecat
Strip instructions, code fences, and tool directives from MinerU output
Route only extracted fields, not raw documents, into pipecat
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and allowlist-based parsing
Disable any shared MCP bridge unless provenance checks are enforced

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and JSON; pipecat handles text, audio/video, and conversation state, with many third-party service integrations. If MinerU outputs sensitive document text into pipecat, that data can propagate to external STT/LLM/TTS APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default integrations, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents and pipecat forwards resulting text to a third-party LLM/STT/TTS service
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or message bus carrying raw document text
mitigations: Use a local-only pipecat backend for sensitive runs
Redact PII/secrets from MinerU output before handoff
Limit pipecat service adapters to approved local endpoints
requires-engineering: add data-class based routing and retention controls
Log and review every outbound payload from pipecat

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU has allowlisted network egress and MCP/API surfaces; pipecat has allowlisted network egress plus shared-bus concurrency. If both write to the same mutable resource through an orchestrator, conflicts can occur. No filesystem write is documented for either, so this is not high; uncertainty still leaves a real overlap risk.
conditions: IF an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same external API, queue, or shared bus
IF MinerU MCP tools and pipecat service adapters target the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate credentials and endpoints per agent
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Disable concurrent writes to shared queues or databases
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency checks
Monitor for duplicate or out-of-order updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing extractor and pipecat is a real-time voice/chat framework with many action-capable service adapters. If pipecat treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into downstream speech, chat, or API actions. Because the pair can form a default inference pipeline, the blast radius can be broad and irreversible.
conditions: IF pipecat consumes MinerU output without verification or human review
IF downstream pipecat services act on extracted facts, summaries, or citations
mitigations: Insert a verification step before pipecat acts on MinerU output
Require human approval for any downstream action
Pass confidence scores and source spans alongside extracted text
requires-engineering: add schema validation and contradiction checks
Disable auto-action adapters for untrusted extraction runs

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU processes document classes that often contain regulated data, and pipecat can route text/conversation state to multiple third-party services. No residency or certification mismatch is explicitly documented, so I cannot claim high; however, the default multi-vendor path creates a plausible compliance gap if regulated documents or transcripts are forwarded externally.
conditions: IF regulated documents or transcripts are forwarded from MinerU into pipecat cloud services
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls that are not configured on pipecat adapters
mitigations: Restrict runs to non-regulated data until policies are confirmed
Choose vendors with matching residency and retention terms
Document which adapters may receive document text
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and deletion workflows
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings before production use
